speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, and weight loss, along with an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. These are significant "B symptoms" that require further investigation. To narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have had any fever episodes or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the pain been localized to a specific area, and have you noticed any change in your stool color, such as it becoming pale or clay-colored? I would also like to know if you have experienced any recent jaundice or itching.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the fixed, non-tender supraclavicular lymph node is indeed concerning, though we must differentiate between tuberculosis and malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Findings show massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT findings of massively enlarged lymph nodes across multiple stations strongly suggest a lymphoproliferative disorder like lymphoma rather than tuberculosis. REQUEST TEST: Excisional lymph node biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cervical Lymph Node Biopsy: Findings show lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing CD20-positive lymphocytes confirm a B-cell malignancy, most likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
